title: Minimum Genetic Mutation
summary: Given a start gene string and an end gene string, both 8 characters long with characters 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T', find the minimum number of single-character mutations needed to transform the start gene into the end gene.
statement: Given a start gene string and an end gene string, both 8 characters long with characters 'A', 'C', 'G', and 'T', find the minimum number of single-character mutations needed to transform the start gene into the end gene. A gene must be listed in a provided gene bank to be valid. If no valid mutation path exists, return -1.
constraints: Genes have exactly eight characters from A,C,G,T; 0 <= bank.length <= 10.
One mutation changes one character. Every reached gene after a change must belong to the bank.
The starting gene is valid even outside the bank. Equal start/end needs zero mutations; return -1 when unreachable.
hints: Treat valid genes as vertices joined by one-character changes.
Breadth-first search finds the fewest edges; only enqueue bank genes not already visited.
Start at distance 0. For each of eight positions try A,C,G,T, enqueue valid unseen strings, and stop at the destination.
The starting state needs no bank entry. With fixed length and alphabet, each bank gene generates a constant number of candidates.
editorial: Every edge costs one mutation, so BFS layers are increasing shortest distances. Generating single-character neighbors enforces edge validity, and a bank set enforces allowed intermediate states. Mark states when enqueuing to avoid repeated cycles. Endpoint differences alone do not prove a route exists or that no detour is needed. An identical start/end has distance zero.

tests.explanation: Changing the final T to A reaches the bank gene in one mutation.
The only route is AA… → GA… → GC… → CC…, taking 3 changes although the endpoints differ in only 2 positions.
